subject: Post-demo: Clearsight dedicated sizing clarifications & GPU recommendations
body_preview: Recap and concrete asks after demo: target TPS, avg/peak token mix, acceptable latency SLO, and preference between A100/H100 for dedicated pool. Attached token profile and initial cost estimate.
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@clearsight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Clearsight dedicated sizing clarifications & GPU recommendations

Thanks again for your time today, Anya — great conversation. Short recap and three concrete clarifying asks so we can finalize a Dedicated pool recommendation that meets your latency & cost targets.

Recap (short)
- Goal: Replace current hosted multi-tenant inference (bursty) with a Dedicated pool for production (latency-sensitive workflows) and remove noisy-neighbor variance.
- Workload shape: mostly synchronous chat completions plus a small async batch job for reranking.
- Quality bar: match current generation quality; we’ll use the same eval set in Redwood Optimize to validate.

Clarifying asks (what we need from Clearsight to size correctly)
1) TPS targets (avg vs peak) — please confirm steady-state TPS and 95th/99th peak. For sizing we need both: e.g., 50 TPS avg, 220 TPS 95th, 400 TPS peak.
2) Token mix — please confirm average prompt tokens and average completion tokens. In the attached spreadsheet I started a token profile; please fill in column B (example UX flows). We use this to estimate KV cache and memory headroom.
3) Latency SLO and acceptable P99 — what latency targets matter for interactive users? If you want <150ms P50 and <400ms P95 that changes batch window and GPU choice.

Initial thoughts from the call (engineering POV)
- If your P95 requirement is lenient (>400ms) and token lengths are short, A100 80GB could be cost-optimal.
- If you need tighter P95/P99 with longer contexts (>4k tokens) we lean H100 or H100 NVL for headroom and lower single-request latency.
- There is an intermediate option: smaller H100 pool + aggressive prefix caching and KV sharing for hot prompts — good for read-heavy prompt patterns.

Attachments:
- clearsight_token_profile.xlsx (please populate the highlighted rows)
- redwood_poc_estimate.pdf (initial committed-capacity estimate — ballpark)

Next steps / ask from you:
- Fill token profile sheet and confirm TPS numbers (avg/95/peak) — if you can get us telemetry export (CSV) that’s ideal.
- State the latency SLO for interactive flows and any blackout windows for batch reranks.

We’ll follow up with a concrete Dedicated pool config (GPU type, pool size, concurrency settings, and recommended batching window) within 24 business hours of the token/TPS numbers. Marissa: can you prepare two baseline configs (A100-focused cost-optimal and H100-focused low-latency) so we can attach them to the POC proposal?

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

From: Anya Petrov <anya@clearsight.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearsight Ops <ops@clearsight.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clearsight dedicated sizing clarifications & GPU recommendations

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers below and I attached the export you requested (token_profile_export.csv) — I also updated the spreadsheet columns you mentioned.

Quick numbers (from Prod telemetry window: last 30 days)
- Avg TPS (chat completions): 42 TPS
- 95th TPS: 190 TPS
- Burst (peak observed): 360 TPS during business-hours demos

Token mix (averages across flows; see attached sheet)
- Avg prompt tokens: 220
- Avg completion tokens: 410
- Long-tail: ~8% of requests exceed 2,000 tokens (user-uploaded context)

Latency SLOs
- Target interactive latency: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 350ms for primary chat endpoint.
- Batch reranks: can tolerate up to 3s, usually scheduled off-peak.

Other constraints/notes
- Data residency: primary infra in us-west; we prefer VPC peering for the POC but don’t need full on-prem for phase 1.
- Cost tradeoff: we’re trying to minimize committed monthly spend but avoid frequent fallbacks to hosted.

Attachments referenced:
- token_profile_export.csv (CSV) — exported telemetry (timestamps anonymized).

Question for Redwood (clarify):
- For the 8% long-tail >2k tokens, would Redwood recommend a separate pool with larger memory GPUs, or a mixed-pool strategy with routing rules?

On that last point: we’re open to a hybrid approach (main pool for 95% traffic + transient large-context nodes for heavy requests) but want to understand cost impact.

Thanks — I’ll file the spreadsheet updates in your Drive link.

Best,
Anya
Head of Product, Clearsight AI
anya@clearsight.ai

---Quoted above: From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: Clearsight dedicated sizing clarifications & GPU recommendations

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding Anya's reply and the telemetry export. Highlights to act on for the POC config:

1) Build two POC configurations to attach to the proposal:
   - Config A (cost-efficient): A100 80GB pool, autoscale headroom to handle 200 TPS sustained, batch window tuned to keep P95 ~350ms. Include prefix caching and 2x KV cache replicas.
   - Config B (latency-first): H100-based pool (NVL flavor if available) sized for 95th 200+ TPS with spare capacity for 360 TPS bursts. Lower batching window, higher concurrency per GPU core.

2) Mixed-pool routing note: include a third transient node pool (larger memory GPUs) that handles requests with context >1500 tokens; route by request header/length. Show cost delta for single vs mixed pool.

3) Deliverables: updated redwood_poc_estimate.pdf with committed pool monthly cost, expected token/unit economics, and recommended fallback policy (hosted fallback during rare overcapacity).

Marissa — can you prioritize Config A/B and a mixed-pool cost sheet? If possible, include expected P50/P95 estimates (simulation) and recommended concurrency settings per model. Also flag any quota or infra constraints for VPC peering mentioned by Clearsight.

I'll wait for your draft and then share with Anya for signoff; target to have a formal proposal by EOD Monday.

—
Ben

Onward.
